title: A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India

content.caseIdentity: A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India, (1969) 2 SCC 262
content.facts: The selection process involved decision-makers whose interests overlapped with the candidates.
questionsBeforeCourt: How far do natural justice rules apply to administrative action?
content.ratioDecidendi: The dividing line between administrative and quasi-judicial power is thin; natural justice applies where fairness requires it and bias is impermissible.
content.holding: The selection process was invalidated for breach of natural justice.
content.relevance: Use for bias and fair administrative procedure.

sources.evidence: Official Supreme Court judgment expressly cites A.K. Kraipak, (1969) 2 SCC 262, and reproduces its paragraph 13 discussion on the thin distinction between administrative and quasi-judicial power and the requirement of fair administrative action.
Official Supreme Court judgment identifies A.K. Kraipak as a Constitution Bench authority and cites paragraph 20 for application of natural justice to administrative decisions.
Discovery copy identifies the 29 April 1969 decision, AIR 1970 SC 150, and reproduces the bias discussion; used for discovery only, not authoritative verification.
